text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — kv-cache continuous-batch amplification detected in prod (region-us-west). 95th p50 token latency rising, eviction rate spiking. paging oncall @maya. details: svc=redwood-runtime kv_cache_evictions=12k/min batch_window=8s -> observed 10x throughput of small requests

sam: on it. @maya you getting the page? i'm checking recent deploys and batchflag state.

maya: got the page. i'm loading dashboards. first pass: errors are low, but tail latency and downstream queue depth are high for several shards. looks correlated with recent change to batch_window default (rolled last night).

lee: fyi i saw a surge of tiny requests from a single tenant (acme-corp) — request-size histogram skewed to 1-3 tokens. KV is filling with lots of tiny prefixes, causing cache amplification.

maya: thanks @lee. can we patch per-tenant batch config to reduce max_batch_window for acme-corp? want to avoid global rollback if possible.

sam: we have a feature-flag gate 'batch_window_dynamic' that can be scoped per-customer. i can flip override for acme-corp to 100ms from 8s. will do a canary on one shard first.

tom: add note: acme-corp is in prod-1 account, shard-7 is hot. doing per-shard canary reduces blast radius.

maya: let's run the mitigation plan: 1) canary override on shard-7 (10% traffic) 2) monitor 5m for tail latency/eviction rate 3) expand to all acme shards if good 4) if not stable, fallback to global batch_window rollback.

sam: executing step 1 now. command: ```
# adminctl feature-flag set batch_window_dynamic --scope=tenant:acme-corp --value=100ms --shard=7 --canary=10%
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: feature-flag update batch_window_dynamic for tenant acme-corp shard-7 (canary 10%). run_id=ff-20260315-01

ops-bot: prometheus alert suppressed for 15m (maintenance window) due to mitigation in progress.

lee: shard-7 canary applied. initial metrics: eviction rate shard-7 down 60% in 90s, p95 latency down 45%. other shards still high.

maya: that's promising. expand to remaining acme shards (shard-7 -> all acme shards) but keep global default unchanged. sam, proceed with gradual rollout across tenant shards at 20% increments.

sam: rolling out to shards 3,5,8 (20% each) now. command: ```
adminctl feature-flag update batch_window_dynamic --scope=tenant:acme-corp --value=100ms --canary=20% --shards=3,5,8
```

deploy-bot: partial rollout in progress. run_id=ff-20260315-02

lee: after shards 3/5/8 went live: aggregate eviction rate for acme down 78%, cluster-wide eviction down 30%, tail latency improving but still jittery in some regions.

maya: good. start targeted traffic shaping for other high-noise tenants (we saw smaller spikes from beta-client and partner-x). apply temporary per-tenant throttle to beta-client at 5rps for 10m.

sam: doing beta-client throttle: ```
adminctl quota set --tenant=beta-client --rate=5rps --duration=10m
```

lee: small-signal experiments show cache pressure drops linearly with reduced tiny-request rate. this confirms root cause.

maya: monitoring for 10 minutes. also coordinating with product to notify acme about degraded tail for 15m window and the fix. @tom send customer comms (brief).

tom: message drafted and sent to acme engineering: "We saw abnormal tiny-request traffic causing cache amplification. We've applied a per-tenant batch-window override reducing max batching for your traffic; latency should improve. We're monitoring and will follow up."

maya: after 12m: all acme shards stable, p95 back to SLA targets, eviction rates restored to baseline. widening suppression.

sam: full rollout complete for acme-corp. flag state: batch_window_dynamic=100ms (tenant scope). recording changelog id=chg-20260315-ff-acme

deploy-bot: rollout complete. run_id=ff-20260315-02 status=success

ops-bot: suppressed alerts cleared.

maya: next steps: 1) keep per-tenant override for acme for 24h, then evaluate whether to make permanent or tune based on real traffic. 2) propose default batch_window downgrade in runtime config but gated behind a gradual global canary — don't want to harm latency for large-batch workloads. 3) add a detection rule to alert on "tiny-request dominant tenant" with tenant-level eviction signal so we can auto-suggest per-tenant overrides earlier.

lee: i'll open a PR for detection rule and add a dashboard panel. sam, can you add the per-tenant rollback/playbook steps to the runbook?

sam: will do. adding notes and exact adminctl commands used into the runbook now. also saving logs: ```
# saved logs
kv_evictions_before.log: https://logs.internal/acme/1987654321/before
kv_evictions_after.log: https://logs.internal/acme/1987654321/after
```

maya: nice work team. will hand this to eng-sre for post-incident analysis. paging clear, leaving thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
